title: Chapter 3 Quiz 7
description: The three kinds of control structure, and the simplest one: sequence.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Match each control structure to what it does.
questions.explanation: The three families of control structures.

questions.question: In a **sequence** structure, execution goes…
options: Back to the first line after each action
Only through the lines whose test is true
In an order chosen randomly at run time
From top to bottom, one statement at a time
questions.explanation: Statements are placed one after the other and run from top to bottom.

questions.question: Put the steps of the algorithm that multiplies two numbers in order.
If we write a ← b and then b ← a, the two values are swapped.
questions.explanation: After a ← b both variables hold b's value, because a's old value is lost. Watch out: a temporary variable is needed.

questions.question: Swap with a temporary variable. Start with a = 3 and b = 7. Fill in the table.
questions.explanation: temp keeps a's old value (3), a takes b (7), then b takes temp (3).

questions.question: Complete the algorithm that swaps a and b.
questions.explanation: Save a in temp, copy b into a, then put the saved value into b.

questions.question: Place the correct shape on each slot of this sequence flowchart.
questions.explanation: Input and output are parallelograms. A calculation is a rectangle.

questions.question: a ← 10, then b ← a, then a ← 20. What is the value of b?
questions.explanation: b received a copy of 10. Changing a afterwards does not change b. Watch out: b is not linked to a.

questions.question: In a sequence structure, the order of the statements does not matter.
questions.explanation: Each statement runs after the one above, so changing the order can change the result. Watch out: swapping two lines of an assignment chain changes the values.
